subject: Zoning Recodification Process
overview: The Planning Department held a workshop to explain the city's zoning amendment procedures and the ongoing effort to recodify Medford's 1960s-era ordinances. Staff clarified that the current initiative focuses on legal alignment and organizational cleanup, while substantive policy changes will follow the completion of the city’s comprehensive plan.

items.title: Zoning Amendment Video Presentation
items.summary: The meeting featured a video presentation outlining the journey of a zoning amendment from initial proposal through public hearings to City Council adoption.

items.title: Mayoral Veto and Approval Authority
items.summary: Legal counsel explained that while the Mayor has veto power over zoning ordinances, the two-thirds council vote required for initial passage matches the threshold needed for a veto override.

items.title: Recodification Purpose and Timeline
items.summary: Staff described the recodification as a cleanup of existing rules to ensure consistency with state law and indicated the document would move through the Community Development Board before returning to the Council in January.

items.title: Explanation of Use and Dimensional Tables
items.summary: Planning staff demonstrated how the city’s use and dimensional tables regulate property activities and building physical requirements, such as height and setbacks.

items.title: Coordination with the Comprehensive Plan
items.summary: Staff clarified that the ongoing comprehensive plan process will likely result in recommendations for substantive zoning policy changes in mid-2023.

items.title: Variances and Non-Conforming Uses
items.summary: The board discussed how older properties are grandfathered as non-conforming uses and reviewed the current legal status of use variances in Medford.
